mechanism: One-time intravitreally delivered recombinant AAV gene therapy using a proprietary capsid and transgene genome encoding the anti-VEGF protein Vb24 for sustained intraocular anti-angiogenic activity.
development_status: NCT05986864 is a recruiting U.S./global Phase 1/2, open-label, non-randomized study of one-time SKG0106 intraocular injection in anti-VEGF-responsive nAMD. A linked China Phase 1 study, NCT06213038, and a 5-year long-term follow-up study, NCT06346600, provide asset context; no FDA approval, BLA filing, Phase 3 trial, or posted ClinicalTrials.gov results were identified.
clinical_summary: SKG0106 is intended to reduce wet AMD treatment burden by replacing frequent anti-VEGF injections with durable intraocular anti-VEGF expression after one intravitreal AAV administration. NCT05986864 enrolls about 68 patients and evaluates DLTs, ocular/systemic AEs, BCVA, CST, VFQ-25, immunogenicity, and PK through 52 weeks. ARVO 2024 interim Phase 1 data from 9 treated Chinese patients reported no supplemental anti-VEGF injections in mid- and high-dose cohorts during reported follow-up, with BCVA improvement or stabilization and CST reduction in those cohorts. Differentiation is meaningful if durability persists, but evidence remains early, open-label, small, and non-comparative.
safety_summary: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT05986864. The study's primary outcomes include DLTs over 4 weeks and ocular/systemic AE type, severity, and incidence over 52 weeks; NCT06346600 follows exposed patients for AEs, SAEs, and AESIs for 5 years post-injection. ARVO 2024 interim Phase 1 data reported no DLTs or treatment-related SAEs in low- and mid-dose cohorts through 30-52 weeks and asymptomatic trace mixed vitreous cells in the high-dose cohort that resolved without intervention. Analog labels support monitoring for ocular/periocular infection, intraocular inflammation, hypersensitivity, endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, intraocular pressure increases, arterial thromboembolic events, retinal vasculitis/vascular occlusion, cataract, retinal abnormalities, visual-acuity decline, and corticosteroid-supported inflammation management.
management_tools: Medical-benefit prior authorization tied to FDA-labeled nAMD criteria, active CNV, eye-level documentation, and retina-specialist administration
Per-eye one-time quantity limit unless future labeling supports retreatment
Requirement for prior anti-VEGF response, high treatment burden, or inadequate durability if final evidence supports post-anti-VEGF positioning
Site-of-care controls for qualified intravitreal gene therapy handling, administration, and post-injection monitoring
Baseline and follow-up documentation of BCVA, OCT/CST, prior injection frequency, rescue injections, and patient-reported visual function
Safety monitoring for ocular inflammation, infection, intraocular pressure, retinal abnormalities/detachment, vascular occlusion, and systemic anti-VEGF thromboembolic risk
Outcomes-based contracting or amortized payment model consideration if launch price resembles one-time ophthalmic gene therapy analogs
Long-term registry or claims surveillance aligned to 5-year follow-up expectations
evidence_gaps: No FDA approval, U.S. prescribing information, BLA filing plan, Phase 3 trial, or direct SKG0106 price was identified.
No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results were identified for NCT05986864, NCT06213038, or NCT06346600.
NCT05986864 remains listed as recruiting in the reviewed ClinicalTrials.gov API snapshot despite estimated January 2026 completion dates.
The ARVO 2024 interim data include only 9 Phase 1 patients with short-to-moderate follow-up and no randomized comparator.
Durability, rescue-injection rates, immunogenicity, inflammation risk, and bilateral-treatment assumptions remain uncertain.
Annual cost estimate uses Luxturna ophthalmic AAV gene therapy analog pricing and may not predict SKG0106 pricing, rebates, administration costs, or outcomes-based payment terms.

sources.title: Positive Interim Results of Intravitreally delivered SKG0106 Phase 1 Clinical Trial in Patients with nAMD
supports: SKG0106 described as a novel recombinant AAV vector for nAMD via intravitreal administration
Vector comprises proprietary capsid and transgene encoding anti-VEGF protein Vb24
Open-label Phase 1 dose-escalation study included 3 dose cohorts of 3 patients each at 8E9, 2.4E10, and 7.2E10 vg/eye
Patients received single intravitreal SKG0106 injection with prophylactic topical corticosteroids tapered over 4 weeks
Nine patients were treated; no DLTs or treatment-related SAEs were detected in low- and mid-dose cohorts up to 30-52 weeks
Asymptomatic trace mixed vitreous cells occurred in the high-dose cohort and resolved without intervention
Mid- and high-dose cohorts showed BCVA improvement or stabilization and mean CST reduction during reported follow-up
No supplemental anti-VEGF injections were needed in the mid- and high-dose cohorts during reported follow-up

sources.title: SKG0106, an AAV vector delivered intravitreally, for effective, safe and durable treatment of nAMD
supports: Preclinical ARVO abstract describes SKG0106 as an intravitreally delivered recombinant AAV vector encoding anti-VEGF protein Vb24
Rabbit and monkey models showed efficacy comparable to Eylea at several doses with longer observed inhibition in some study windows
Monkey long-term prophylactic CNV study reported strong efficacy at 26 weeks while Eylea did not show inhibitory effect on lesions in that model
No AEs were detected in the reported preclinical pharmacodynamic studies and no systemic abnormal findings were detected in pharmacodynamic studies or a GLP monkey toxicity study
Authors state INDs for SKG0106 had been approved in the U.S. and China and clinical trial was ongoing

sources.title: VABYSMO (faricimab-svoa) Prescribing Information
supports: Vabysmo is indicated for neovascular wet AMD and administered by intravitreal injection
Recommended nAMD dosing starts every 4 weeks for the first 4 doses followed by OCT and visual-acuity evaluations with interval adjustment
Contraindications include ocular or periocular infection, active intraocular inflammation, and hypersensitivity
Warnings include endophthalmitis and retinal detachments, intraocular pressure increases, arterial thromboembolic events, and retinal vasculitis/vascular occlusion
Common adverse reactions include cataract and conjunctival hemorrhage

sources.title: LUXTURNA (voretigene neparvovec-rzyl) Prescribing Information
supports: Luxturna is an adeno-associated virus vector-based ocular gene therapy
Luxturna is administered once per eye and recommends peri-administration systemic corticosteroids
Warnings include endophthalmitis, permanent decline in visual acuity, retinal abnormalities, intraocular pressure increases, intraocular air bubble precautions, and cataract

Common adverse reactions include conjunctival hyperemia, cataract, increased intraocular pressure, retinal tear, macular hole, subretinal deposits, eye inflammation, eye irritation, eye pain, and maculopathy
Used as an ocular AAV gene therapy safety-management analog for SKG0106

expected_launch_window.method: Used NCT05986864 Phase 1/2 recruiting status, estimated 2026 completion dates without posted results, NCT06346600 5-year follow-up through March 2031, absence of identified Phase 3/filing, and early interim Phase 1 evidence.
expected_launch_window.explanation: SKG0106 is clinically active but still early. Without a pivotal Phase 3 or filing signal, a U.S. launch before 2030 is unlikely; long-term follow-up reinforces unresolved safety and durability questions.

annual_cost_range.method: No SKG0106 price was found. Used Luxturna, the approved ophthalmic AAV gene therapy analog, at $850,000 per one-time bilateral treatment; low assumes one treated eye at half the bilateral cost, and high assumes both eyes treated in the first year. Vabysmo price is included only as current chronic intravitreal benchmark context.
annual_cost_range.explanation: SKG0106 is a one-time ocular AAV therapy, so a one-time per-eye gene therapy analog is more relevant than annualizing chronic anti-VEGF injections. Final SKG0106 price could differ materially based on durability, bilateral use, outcomes-based contracts, rebates, and administration costs.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted one-time intravitreal AAV anti-VEGF mechanism, early rescue-free mid/high dose signal, BCVA/CST stabilization or improvement, and long-term follow-up design against small sample size, open-label design, and lack of randomized pivotal data.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Durable intravitreal anti-VEGF expression could materially reduce injection burden, but available efficacy and safety evidence is too immature for a High rating.

budget_impact.method: Combined ophthalmic AAV analog one-time cost with a potentially broad nAMD population and medical-benefit/site-of-care complexity.
budget_impact.explanation: Even if restricted to anti-VEGF-experienced or high-burden patients, a per-eye one-time therapy priced like Luxturna would create concentrated claim exposure and demand outcomes-based management.

disruption_risk.method: Balanced high potential to reduce chronic intravitreal injections and alter retina buy-and-bill workflows against early development status, no approval, no direct price, and availability of established anti-VEGF management policies.
disruption_risk.explanation: A durable one-time therapy could disrupt injection frequency, site-of-care economics, and payment design, but near-term disruption is moderated by early clinical maturity and uncertain launch timing.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to Phase 1/2 status, absence of posted results or filing, long-term follow-up through 2031, and early but notable durability signal.
recommended_action.explanation: Track NCT05986864 updates, full Phase 1/2 data, rescue-injection durability, ocular inflammation signals, Phase 3 initiation, and any gene-therapy payment model signals. Formal coverage build is premature before pivotal evidence and label details.

quality_flags: This packet is keyed to NCT05986864, the Phase 1/2 interventional parent study; NCT06346600 is included only as linked long-term follow-up context.
No direct SKG0106 price found; annual cost estimate uses Luxturna ophthalmic AAV gene therapy analog pricing.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT05986864, NCT06213038, or NCT06346600.
Interim efficacy and safety evidence is based on a small open-label Phase 1 abstract with 9 treated patients and no randomized comparator.
NCT05986864 remains listed as recruiting in the reviewed ClinicalTrials.gov API snapshot despite estimated January 2026 completion dates.
No Phase 3, BLA filing, FDA label, or U.S. launch date was identified.
